boundary_decision.rationale: The publication case is a defensible aggregate root for one governed publication operation. It owns the operation identifier, target binding, decisions, instructions, attempts, observations and change history while external masters retain content, edition, actor, channel, rights and evidence identity. The frozen record-plane classifier remains standalone-mm.

decisions.rationale: The scope and five boundary notes consistently separate the governed operation from content, edition, actor, platform, rights, communication, analytics and record masters. Stable case lineage and non-cascade rules permit accountable coordination without absorbing those lifecycles.

decisions.concept: Approval, instruction, delivery and availability separation
decisions.rationale: Separate findings, artifacts and functions distinguish editorial decisions, immutable release instructions, origin and downstream delivery attempts, acknowledgements and independently timed availability observations. HTTP success and syndication are explicitly rejected as proof of audience reach or origin authority.

decisions.concept: Correction, retraction, withdrawal and takedown succession
decisions.rationale: The governed-change layer, change-or-remove function, patch rules and lifecycle artifacts jointly define the invariant: released decisions, instructions and evidence are immutable; a correction or removal action creates a separately identified successor instruction and notice, preserves the affected release binding and records propagation verification.

The identity priority is an explicit policy hierarchy: use a source-qualified authoritative master-system publication-case identifier, otherwise a governed resolvable case IRI, otherwise a Dimension UUID. Namespace guidance requires minting identifiers for case, instruction, delivery, observation, notice and event records. Concrete algorithms and resolvers belong to the adopting Dimension profile rather than this format-neutral specification.

The candidate parent is metadata, not an approved registry edge. The model remains coherent because it requires an external edition or content binding by reference and does not claim edition ownership. Later registry work may approve inheritance or replace it with an explicit reference contract. This limits relationship-completeness claims but does not block a standalone reviewable draft.

Default-deny access covers embargoed content, personal data, confidential drafts, credentials, legal review and restricted analytics. Access is enforceable at bundle, layer, finding and artifact scopes, exceptions require authority and audit, and eight roles separate duties. Concrete confidentiality labels and role bindings remain mandatory in the adopting Dimension policy profile.

Fifteen official primary specifications ground protocol, metadata, provenance, accessibility, language, rights, annotation, discovery and timestamp semantics. Protocol standards are not represented as editorial or legal policy, and Sitemaps is limited to a discovery projection.
